newsitem.title: CHINA: China urges strict supervision of futures trading.
newsitem.headline: China urges strict supervision of futures trading.

text.p: China's top securities watchdog has urged local securities regulatory bodies and futures firms to more strictly supervise futures trading to check rampant irregularities, the Shanghai Securities News said on Saturday.

The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), in an urgent notice on September 24, said there were serious problems such as lax management and financial disorder in futures brokerages, disregard for professional standards, inadequate control of risk, and frequent litigation because of disputes, the newspaper said.

In the notice, the CSRC re-affirmed that futures brokerages or authorised firms doing futures business must not entrust individuals or other companies to trade futures on their behalf. All such contracts must be cancelled within 30 days of the CSRC order on September 24, the notice said.
All futures companies must conduct an internal audit within 30 days of the issue of the notice and must report the results of the audit to the CSRC, it said.

As from the fourth quarter of 1996, all the firms must conduct internal audits every three months and report the results to local securities bodies, as well as the CSRC, within 15 days of the end of each quarter.
The notice re-affirmed that only authorised futures brokerages could conduct futures business and these brokerages must apply to the CSRC if they want to open new branches.
Violators would be fined and those guilty of serious offences would have their futures licences revoked, the notice said.
Those who committed crimes would have their cases referred to the public security and judicial departments, it said.
